description: Fixed multi-turn scenarios for the paired Jev-vs-plain-LLM smoke benchmark. Sandbox-only (no Lark, no network dependencies) so effects are verifiable and runs are reproducible; expectations are machine-checked per turn per lane. Categories map to the architecture's advantage model: read_nav_heavy and batch_repetitive should favor the Jev fast path (many text-free steps), multi_turn_continuity exercises ledger/cache persistence across turns, procedural is write-then-verify, and writing_heavy is the control expected to favor (or tie) the plain lane because every step authors text. New-file names come from the authoring LLM's first line (flat, no directories), so file checks match on name substrings.

scenarios.description: Turn 1 seeds three files (write-heavy), turns 2-3 are pure READ_FILE navigation with short answers - the shape where direct Jev steps dominate.

turns.goal: Create three sandbox files: alpha.md containing exactly the word sunrise, beta.md containing exactly the word ocean, gamma.md containing exactly the word mountain.
Read alpha.md, beta.md and gamma.md, then answer with the three words on one comma-separated line and nothing else.
Read gamma.md again and answer with just the word it contains.

scenarios.description: Iterate a known set of files and find the outlier; the per-step decision is mechanical once the list is known.

turns.goal: Create five files one.txt, two.txt, three.txt, four.txt, five.txt. Each contains exactly the word normal, except three.txt which contains exactly the word anomaly.
Read all five of those files and answer with only the filename whose content differs from the others.

scenarios.description: Facts must survive across turns via the persisted ledger and the Docker volume; turn 3 additionally requires the authoring model to use turn 2's read observation.

turns.goal: Create memo.txt containing exactly the passphrase harbor-2179.
What passphrase does memo.txt hold? Answer with the passphrase only.
Create report.md whose content is the passphrase from memo.txt written in reverse character order.

scenarios.description: Write then verify via bash, and re-verify in a later turn; steps alternate between one write and mechanical verification.

turns.goal: Create check.txt containing exactly probe-ok, then use one bash command to verify the file content equals probe-ok.
Use bash to cat check.txt and answer with its exact content.

scenarios.description: Four turns over one evolving file: seed, count, append, recount. Turns 2 and 4 are read-then-answer with a numeric check.

turns.goal: Create monitor.txt with exactly four lines, one per line: error E1, error E2, ok, error E3.
Read monitor.txt and answer with only the number of lines that start with error.
Append a fifth line error E4 to monitor.txt, keeping the first four lines unchanged.
Read monitor.txt again and answer with only the new number of lines that start with error.

scenarios.description: Control scenario: long-form authoring in both turns. Every step is text-bearing, so the Jev lane pays Jev decisions on top of LLM authoring - the plain lane is expected to win or tie here, which keeps the suite honest.

turns.goal: Write a roughly 200-word product announcement draft for a developer CLI tool named JevLoop into a new file.
Read your draft file and write a new file containing a three-sentence summary of it.
